items.followUp: State two aims of Pakistan’s National Conservation Strategy.

rubric.why: Identifies the strategy and its national context.
rubric.description: Names Pakistan’s National Conservation Strategy and its adoption in 1992.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the NCS as Pakistan’s strategy adopted in 1992.

rubric.why: States the strategy’s biodiversity conservation aim.
rubric.description: Conservation of biodiversity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that biodiversity or biological resources are to be conserved.

rubric.why: States that biological resources should be used sustainably.
rubric.description: Sustainable use of biological resources.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning sustainable use of biological resources.

rubric.why: Includes fair sharing of benefits from biological resources.
rubric.description: Fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from biological resources.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that benefits should be shared fairly or equitably.

modelAnswer: Pakistan’s National Conservation Strategy (NCS), adopted in 1992, provides a framework for conserving natural resources.
It aims to conserve biodiversity and biological resources.
It promotes the sustainable use of biological resources.
It supports the fair and equitable sharing of benefits obtained from these resources.

items.followUp: Compare aerobic and anaerobic respiration, and give one example of anaerobic respiration.

rubric.why: Distinguishes the processes by oxygen requirement.
rubric.description: Aerobic respiration requires oxygen; anaerobic respiration occurs without oxygen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly contrasting oxygen requirement.

rubric.why: Distinguishes the extent of glucose breakdown.
rubric.description: Aerobic respiration completely breaks down glucose; anaerobic respiration breaks it down incompletely.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for contrasting complete and incomplete breakdown.

rubric.why: Contrasts the products and relative energy yield.
rubric.description: Gives appropriate products and indicates that anaerobic respiration releases less energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct product/energy contrast, such as aerobic respiration yielding carbon dioxide, water and more energy.

rubric.why: Explains the conditions and site of anaerobic respiration.
rubric.description: Explains that anaerobic respiration is the breakdown of glucose without oxygen in the cytoplasm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the process as glucose breakdown without oxygen; accept the cytoplasm as its site.

rubric.why: Shows an appropriate outcome of anaerobic respiration in an organism or tissue.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example: yeast produces ethanol and carbon dioxide, or muscle cells produce lactic acid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either correct example and its product(s).

modelAnswer: Aerobic respiration requires oxygen, whereas anaerobic respiration takes place without oxygen.
Aerobic respiration completely breaks down glucose; anaerobic respiration breaks it down incompletely.
Aerobic respiration produces carbon dioxide and water and releases more energy; anaerobic respiration releases less energy.
Anaerobic respiration is the incomplete breakdown of glucose without oxygen in the cytoplasm.
In yeast it produces ethanol and carbon dioxide; in muscle cells it produces lactic acid.

items.followUp: Name the three types of muscle tissue and state whether each is voluntary or involuntary.

rubric.why: Describes the basic function of muscle tissue.
rubric.description: Muscle tissue consists of contractile cells that produce movement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its ability to contract and bring about movement.

rubric.why: Identifies skeletal muscle and its control.
rubric.description: Skeletal (striated) muscle is voluntary.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming skeletal or striated muscle and identifying it as voluntary.

rubric.why: Identifies smooth muscle and its control.
rubric.description: Smooth (non-striated) muscle is involuntary.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming smooth or non-striated muscle and identifying it as involuntary.

rubric.why: Identifies cardiac muscle and its control.
rubric.description: Cardiac muscle is involuntary and is found in the heart.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying cardiac muscle as involuntary; accept mention of the heart.

modelAnswer: Muscle tissue is made of cells that contract and produce movement.
Skeletal or striated muscle is usually attached to bones and is voluntary.
Smooth or non-striated muscle is found in the walls of internal organs and is involuntary.
Cardiac muscle is found in the heart and is involuntary.

rubric.why: Includes the relationship between physics and biological study.
rubric.description: Biophysics is the application of the principles and methods of physics to the study of living organisms or biological processes.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for a definition that connects physics principles or methods with the study of biology; award 1 mark if only one side of this connection is clear.

modelAnswer: Biophysics is the application of the principles and methods of physics to the study of living organisms and biological processes.

items.followUp: Write the scientific names of wheat and the housefly.

rubric.why: Checks the scientific name of mustard.
rubric.description: Mustard is Brassica campestris.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct scientific name of mustard.

rubric.why: Checks the scientific name of frog.
rubric.description: The frog is Rana tigrina (also accepted: Hoplobatrachus tigerinus).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either the textbook name or the currently used scientific name.

modelAnswer: The scientific name of mustard is Brassica campestris.
The scientific name of frog is Rana tigrina.

items.followUp: What is an ecosystem, and where does it fit in the levels of biological organization?

rubric.why: Identifies the highest level of organization.
rubric.description: The biosphere is the highest level in the levels of organization of organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the biosphere.

rubric.why: Defines the biosphere rather than only naming it.
rubric.description: The biosphere includes all ecosystems or the parts of Earth where life exists.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the biosphere as all ecosystems or the life-supporting parts of Earth.

modelAnswer: The biosphere is the highest level in the levels of organization of organisms.
It includes all ecosystems and the parts of Earth where life exists.

items.followUp: State one characteristic that makes a hypothesis scientifically useful.

rubric.why: Describes the tentative nature of a hypothesis.
rubric.description: A hypothesis is a tentative or possible explanation for observations.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a hypothesis as a tentative explanation or proposed answer.

rubric.why: States that a hypothesis can be examined scientifically.
rubric.description: A hypothesis must be testable, for example through observations or experiments.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it can be tested or verified by investigation.

modelAnswer: A hypothesis is a tentative explanation for observations or a possible answer to a scientific question.
It must be testable through observations or experiments.

items.followUp: Why is a control group included in a scientific experiment?

rubric.why: Distinguishes the control group from the group receiving the treatment.
rubric.description: The control group is not exposed to the factor being tested, while other conditions are kept comparable.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the control group does not receive the treatment or tested factor.

rubric.why: Explains how the control group helps interpret the experiment.
rubric.description: It provides a standard for comparison to determine the effect of the tested factor.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining its role as a comparison or reference group.

modelAnswer: A control group is kept under the same conditions as the experimental group but does not receive the factor being tested.
It provides a standard for comparison so that the effect of the tested factor can be identified.
